question: Which of the following states of India still uses the ancient bamboo drip irrigation method?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya** still uses the ancient **bamboo drip irrigation method**, which is a traditional method of irrigation that involves the use of **bamboo pipes** to supply water to crops. 
 
• Meghalaya's **unique topography**, with its hills and valleys, makes it well-suited for this method of irrigation as it allows for the** collection and distribution** of water to different levels of the terrain.
 
• This method is **eco-friendly, cost-effective,** and sustainable as it uses locally available resources and does not require electricity or fuel to operate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana** primarily uses modern irrigation methods such as **sprinkler and drip irrigation. **
 
• **Maharashtra **also primarily uses **modern irrigation methods,** although some farmers may still use traditional methods on a small scale.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** primarily uses** canal irrigation** and **tube wells** for irrigation purposes.
 
• Bamboo drip irrigation is also known as the** "jingkieng ksiar"** method in Meghalaya and has been used for centuries by the** Khasi tribe.**
 
• The bamboo pipes used in this method are **perforated with small holes **to allow water to drip slowly onto the roots of the crops.
 
• Other traditional methods of irrigation used in India include the use of **bullock carts **to draw water from wells, the construction of **earthen embankments** to create ponds and the use of traditional water harvesting structures such as** stepwells and baolis.**
